# Study design and data contracts

## Cohorts and ascertainment

The historical conventional-testing cohort and the ONT report cohort are different
patient groups in the available extracts. Both are referral cohorts and are
therefore enriched for positive or clinically suspicious cases. Their observed
variant distributions depend on referral indication, calendar period, assay menu,
reporting policy, nationality mix and age structure.

The unit of analysis must be explicit. Counts of people, specimens, analysis
episodes, reports, findings, alleles, chromosome haplotypes and diploid genotypes
are not interchangeable. Repeat testing and family relationships must be retained
where available.

## Provenance-preserving report model

`normalise_cohort_reports.py` converts a declared report export into three tables:
analysis episodes, reported findings and phenotype measurements. Raw report wording
is preserved beside normalized fields. Blank cells remain `not_reported`; only an
explicit sentinel becomes `not_tested`. Neither state is converted to a wild-type
call.

## Analysis eligibility

Every outcome analysis requires an explicit denominator and missingness rule. Hb,
MCV, MCH, HbA2 and HbF can have different eligible subsets and measurement dates.
The term *clinical severity* should be reserved for a genuine outcome such as
transfusion dependence, treatment class or hospitalization; otherwise the analysis
concerns haematological phenotype.
